entities.name: World War II Era
entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary:
The World War II Era, spanning approximately 1939 CE to 1945 CE, represents the most devastating global conflict in human history. This timeframe, a pivotal sub-period of the broader Modern era, fundamentally reshaped geopolitical landscapes and societal structures worldwide. It is characterized by unprecedented scale, technological advancement in warfare, and ideological clashes between the Axis powers (primarily Germany, Italy, and Japan) and the Allies (including the United Kingdom, United States, Soviet Union, and China).

Key events during this era include Germany's Blitzkrieg campaigns across Europe, the Battle of Britain, the attack on Pearl Harbor in December 1941, the systematic genocide of the Holocaust, the D-Day landings in Normandy in June 1944, and the final capitulation of Japan following the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945. Military innovations such as radar, jet aircraft, and code-breaking played crucial roles, while civilian populations endured widespread suffering, forced labor, and mass casualties, estimated at 70 to 85 million deaths.
